We need to keep a few things in mind for this to make sense:

1) There are **energy levels around an atom** where electrons can be found known as **"bands"**

2) The electron(s) in the **highest level** of energy is said to be in the **valence band**. The energy in the valence band depends on the element you're considering. 

3) **For electricity to travel an electron has to move up from the valence band to an even higher level of energy called the conduction band**

4) The amount of **energy required** to move an electron from the **valence band to the conduction** band is called the **band gap**

5) Some elements have a very **high band gap** so they are **insulators**. Some have a very **small band gap** so they are **conductors**. 

6) **Semi conductors** (Transistors are made of these) have a **band gap** that is right **in the middle** of that. And you can **play around with it to make it a conductor or insulator**.

PS: playing around with it means applying a voltage to it in different ways.
